summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY with embedded software experience in bare-metal C on STM32 microcontrollers, FreeRTOS, and UART/I2C/SPI communication. Built real-time firmware with interrupt-driven peripherals and debugged it at the hardware level with oscilloscopes and logic analyzers. Integrated sensors, servos, and multi-board controllers (STM32, Arduino, Jetson) into working hardware/software systems, including a robotic arm that reached 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials).

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth, translating 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands in Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.
Led a 25-member robotics team across national-level competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and AI/ML integration end-to-end.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed a Python GUI using PyQt and Matplotlib for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization in a laboratory environment.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built Cortex-M4 firmware in bare-metal embedded C on an STM32 microcontroller, achieving 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified in Proteus.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver.
Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1) with timer-synchronized sensing and real-time display.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Built an STM32 real-time controller running FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination, driven by YOLOv8 detections from an NVIDIA Jetson over UART.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands and user override; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Built a voice-controlled, vision-guided robotic pick-and-place system with a Jetson + Arduino controller (two-link IK in C++, five servos); achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials).
Resolved 11 hardware/software integration failures (servo brown-out, stale-frame capture); integrated dual VL53L0X ToF sensors over a TCA9548A I2C mux for gripper close at 25 mm.
Deployed the Jetson-side arm bridge as a systemd service (auto-restart with backoff, non-root isolation) with static IP networking.
